description:
FOUND s438h (Opus 5) while widening the interpolation side (#451), and
PRE-EXISTING in the CODE path: identical on a cf0076c worktree.

  @! = (11,22,33);
  print "C:", $![1], " S:$![1]\n";     # perl: C:22 S:22
                                       # PCL:  C:   S:      (HEAD: C:  S:[1])

  Emission: (p-aref (p-errno-string) 1)      <- the SCALAR $!, indexed
  Compare:  (p-aref @? 1)                    <- what every other member gives

EVERY OTHER MEMBER OF THE FAMILY IS RIGHT in both paths after #451 -- measured
one character at a time against perl 5.40.3, `@X = (11,22,33); print "C:",
$X[1], " S:$X[1]"`:

    ? . / ~ & % = < >    C:22 S:22   both agree with perl
    !                    C:   S:     both wrong, this task

So the rule "a `[` after a punctuation name subscripts the punctuation ARRAY"
is implemented everywhere except where a competing SCALAR special claims the
name first.  `$!` is the one with an accessor (`p-errno-string`, task #144's
subject); the others have no such shortcut, which is why they fall through to
the element rule correctly.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW: before #451 the STRING path left `[1]` literal (`S:[1]`),
so the two paths disagreed and the string half looked like the only bug.  With
the string path fixed they agree -- and agree on the wrong answer, which is
what makes this a task rather than a footnote.

FIX SHAPE: the element rule must be asked BEFORE the scalar-special accessor
for a punctuation name followed by a subscript -- i.e. the same discriminator
`$-[0]`/`$+[0]` already use, applied where `$!` is turned into
`(p-errno-string)`.  Grep for the sibling copy first (CLAUDE.md 11): the
`$!`-to-accessor rewrite may exist at more than one site, and #144 (`\$!` needs
the magic-cell box) is in the same neighbourhood -- if #144 lands first, `$!`
becomes a box and this rule changes shape with it.

BAR: the ten-character matrix above (both paths) as the acceptance table; a row
in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t beside #451's; corpus-diff + the four-population
A/B; the sweep if emission moves.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `$![1]` is the ERRNO STRING indexed, not an element of @! -- the `$!` scalar special is consulted before the punctuation-array element rule, in the CODE path (the string path now agrees with it, which is how it was found)
